chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim the exegete, al-Jarjani, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us; he said: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Husayni narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Nasiri, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father, al-Rida, from his father, Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father, Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, al-Husayn (peace be upon them).

It was said to the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him): Describe death to us. He said: You have fallen upon the acquainted. It is one of three things that will approach a person: either a glad tidings of the bliss of eternity, or a glad tidings of the torment of eternity, or grief and horror with an ambiguous matter, not knowing from which group he is. As for our ally, the obedient to our command, he is the one given glad tidings of the bliss of eternity. As for our enemy who opposes us, he is the one given glad tidings of the torment of eternity. As for the one whose matter is ambiguous, who does not know his condition, he is the believer who is extravagant towards himself, not knowing what his condition will lead to. The news comes to him ambiguous and frightening, then Allah, Exalted and Glorious, will not equate him with our enemies, but He will take him out of the Fire by our intercession. So act and obey, do not be complacent and do not belittle the punishment of Allah, Exalted and Glorious, for indeed, among those who are extravagant, there is one whom our intercession will not reach except after a torment of three hundred thousand years.
ai.seo_question: What are the three possible outcomes of death according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and how does intercession affect the extravagant believer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* categorizes death into three distinct eschatological outcomes, highlighting the nuanced status of the *Musrif* (extravagant believer) who faces an ambiguous fate. It emphasizes that while the obedient are guaranteed Paradise and the enemies Hell, the *Musrif* undergoes purification through the intercession of the Ahl al-Bayt, with some enduring up to 300,000 years of punishment. This reflects the Shia doctrine of *Tawassul* and the efficacy of the Imams' intercession in mitigating divine justice for those who strayed but remained within the fold.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	We were told by Muhammed bin Qasem, the exegete, al-Jarjani, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Ahmad bin Hasan al-Hussaini, from Hasan bin Ali al-Nasiri, from his father, from Muhammed bin Ali, from his father, al-Rida, from his father, Musa bin Ja’far, from his father, Ja’far bin Muhammed, from his father, Muhammed bin Ali, from his father, Ali bin Hussain, from his father, Hussain, peace be upon them, that he said:

It was said to the Commander of the Believers, peace be upon him: Describe death to us. He said: You have fallen upon the acquainted. It is one of three things that will approach a person: either it is a glad tiding of the bliss of the everlasting; or a news of the torment of the everlasting; or causing of grief and horror, by which one’s matter is unclear and he does not know from which group he is. As for our ally, the obedient to our cause, he is the one to be given glad tidings of the bliss of the everlasting. As for our enemy who opposes us, he is to be given news of the torment of the everlasting. As for the one who does not know his condition, he is the believer who was thriftless towards himself and does not know what his condition will lead to. He will be reached by news that leave him in a state of unclarity and fear. Furthermore, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, will not level him with our enemies, however, He will take him out of the Fire by our salvation. Hence, act and obey, do not have confidence from nor belittle the punishment of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, for indeed, among the thriftless are those whom our salvation will not save except after the torment of three hundred thousand years.
